Add `Jp2DecodeStats`" genuinely begins with the paragraph "Do not start by optimizing `MqDecoder`...", and import::extract_markdown takes the section body's first paragraph verbatim, exactly as documented and as its tests pin. The importer was faithful; a discursive document's first paragraph is simply a poor summary of its own heading. What remains, and it is real: `akr import` drafts one record per heading with no threshold and no review gate, and import::classify defaults every heading that matches none of its five keyword rules to `work`. Its own comment gives the rationale — "a `proposed` work record asserts nothing normative" — which is true about normativity and false about the work queue, because a proposed work record is rendered in ACTIVE-WORK.md and reads as a live commitment. Importing the five lege-codecs/jp2lam/decode-fix-plan documents in 2026-08 therefore minted 125 live proposed work records, including pure report prose ("Executive verdict", "Wall times (median of 5 runs)", "Peak RSS, single representative run", "Reproduce", "Audit limitations", "1. Objective", "6. Quick reference") and negative guidance ("Do not start with", "Two traps - do NOT fix these by loosening a check"). The result was a 1291-line ACTIVE-WORK.md nobody could use, and clearing it took 125 separate `akr abandon` calls. The sharp part is that AKR already ships the fix and `import` does not mention it: `akr ingest` is a review-gated path with preview, per-candidate dispositions and apply. Nothing in `akr import --help` points at it or warns what a discursive document will produce. Also worth noting: the importer sets neither `watches` nor `scope` on anything it drafts, so it is not the source of the mis-shaped watch globs seen in other bulk-ported ledgers.  `@lege-ecosystem.papercut.akr-import-ingest-of-a-long-planning-document/3`

- [closed 2026-11-04] [dk] (akr) Evidence records routinely cite `.agent/scratch` paths as their `artifact`, but scratch is documented as prunable and nothing stops a cited path being deleted: 38 records across 5 .akr files reference `.agent/scratch/...`. Most are already dangling — when `.agent/scratch/ocr-benchmark` was inspected on 2026-08-22 it held only score.py, b3.*, target/ and three recipe output dirs, while eight separate evidence records cite sibling paths under it (tensorrt-smoke-*, lazy-corrected-*, out-winocr-12mp-200-sharded, release-auto-winocr-*, release-tensorrt-*, turboocr-*.txt) that had already been pruned. Those verified claims silently lost their backing. The fix belongs in `knowledge.evidence_add`: it should refuse an `artifact` path under the scratch root outright, at write time, and tell the author to move the artefact somewhere durable first. Refusing at the point of writing is what makes the guarantee hold — a warning emitted later by `akr build` or `validate` arrives after the record is already in the ledger, and by then the usual outcome is a dangling reference nobody re-reads. A durable-path precondition is cheap to check and turns an unenforced convention into an invariant.  `@lege-ecosystem.papercut.evidence-records-routinely-cite-agent-scratch/3`
- [closed 2026-10-06] (A test that shells out to an external tool through a shared temp path is only safe if the path is unique per call, not per process -- the Rust harness's default is threads in one process, not one process per test.) tests/page_parallel_test.rs produced an intermittent `ddjvu failed to decode page 1` under load. Its three tests run on threads of one process, but assert_decodes_with_page_count wrote its scratch document to a path keyed only on std::process::id(), so two tests wrote different documents to the same file and handed it to ddjvu; whichever lost the race decoded the other's document. Fixed by adding a per-call sequence number to the path and cleaning up on success.  `@lege-ecosystem.papercut.djvu-page-parallel-test-shared-a-pid-keyed-scratch-path/2`
